checkpoints.description: App binary launches under tauri-driver and a WebDriver session attaches to its WebView
The WebView renders a <body> element
The WebView loads a document with a non-empty URL (the platform shell or the offline fallback)
The document exposes a non-empty title
The LLM picker merges on-device (local) models with the provider's cloud models in one availability-ranked list
A not-installed on-device model pulls via the download_model IPC and streams live progress events (real smollm:135m pull against the compiled binary)
Cancelling an in-flight pull returns promptly and the app keeps answering IPC (the no-freeze regression fix)
Clicking a different on-device model while one is downloading shows the 'already downloading' notice (one pull at a time)
A completed pull installs the on-device model (check_ollama_status lists it); the selection UI is covered by odm-06
The nav-bar on-device badge reflects the selected local model
check_opencode_status reports Code readiness (installed / version / config_ready / sandboxed / supported / sandbox_ready)
install_opencode downloads and installs the pinned opencode release binary (live)
The freshly installed binary is discoverable on the augmented PATH — status reports installed with a version instead of re-downloading forever
A chat with real work keeps its own workspace under the app-managed root; an untouched leftover (just .git) is recycled for the next chat instead of stranding one dir per launch
A chat keeps the same workspace across calls, persisted in workspaces.json
The folder picker repoints ONE chat at an arbitrary path and leaves other chats untouched
opencode_close / opencode_permission_respond on an unknown id are graceful no-ops
The app keeps answering IPC while opencode downloads and extracts (setup-freeze regression)
set_opencode_skills materialises a mentor’s Agent Skills as SKILL.md packages (frontmatter + text resources), with hostile slugs/filenames confined to the staging dir
A skills rewrite drops deselected skills, an empty sync clears the tree, and `skills: null` ends a sync without touching it
ensure_vibe_skills installs the shared iblai/vibe skill set into the app data dir (live tarball fetch, daily sha-gated)
A permission prompt in one chat does not block another chat's turn
The 5-session cap evicts the least-recently-used idle opencode process
The permission prompt renders in the chat that raised it
The Code pill spins in place of its icon while skills sync, and the popover shows the amber note when the sync fails
A Code turn invokes a synced skill through opencode’s native skill tool (permission card, then skill content in context)
New Chat in the sidebar evicts the previous chat’s opencode process while Code is on
A Code turn’s opencode process runs inside the OS sandbox (bwrap / sandbox-exec) — only the workspace and tool caches writable, ~/.ssh empty
A second New Chat in one app run gets its own fresh workspace, and a chat’s folder follows it from the ephemeral first-turn key to its real session id

Killing the opencode process mid-turn: the answer continues in the same bubble with no visible interruption (one silent respawn re-sends the prompt), and a second kill in the same turn surfaces ollama:error
The Code approval mode (manual/auto) round-trips through ~/.local/share/iblai/settings.json, survives a restart, and an unknown mode is refused rather than defaulting
A mentor keeps one workspace across chats while another mentor gets its own, and New Workspace mints a fresh folder without deleting the previous one
The Code popover asks for an approval mode on first use and stores the answer against the signed-in user (so it follows them to another machine)
The Code popover offers New Workspace and a platform-named Open Folder button (Finder / Explorer / the probed Linux file manager)

A between-turn opencode death (crash, idle reap, LRU eviction) is invisible: the next turn session/loads the same conversation back, and when a load isn't possible the frontend's transcript is resent so the agent continues; a mid-turn death keeps the input busy — the Stop button stays Stop and no suggested prompts appear while the backend silently respawns
A managed opencode older than the pinned version is re-downloaded at boot; a user's own PATH copy is never replaced
